# Metrics reference

Every instrument this build exports, straight from the catalogue the exporter describes itself with. Nothing here is hand-maintained: a metric that is emitted but missing from this page fails the build.

Exports are off by default. Set `telemetry.prometheus = true` and scrape `telemetry.metrics_listen` (default `127.0.0.1:9090`), which is a **separate, unauthenticated** listener — see [monitoring](monitoring.md) for the scrape config, the alert rules, and why it is not a route on the application port.

## `http_requests_total`

*counter*

Labels: `route`, `method`, `status`

HTTP requests answered, by matched route, method and status code. `route` is the router's matched path or one of the bounded fallbacks `{api}`, `{pub}`, `{asset}` — never the raw URI, which an anonymous caller could otherwise choose.

## `http_request_duration_seconds`

*histogram*

Labels: `route`, `method`, `status`

Time to the response head, in seconds. Excludes streaming bodies: an archive download's head is written long before its last byte.

## `rate_limit_trips_total`

*counter*

Labels: `limit`

Requests refused by a rate limit, by bucket family. This is the volume signal: the audit log records one row per bucket per window, deliberately, so it cannot be filled by the traffic it refuses.

## `rate_limit_fallback_total`

*counter*

Labels: `bucket`

Auth-abuse limit decisions taken by this instance's in-process fallback because the KV was unreachable (S-24.e). Non-zero means the shared limiter is down and the effective budget is per instance — up to N x the limit across N replicas.

## `publishes_total`

*counter*

Labels: `format`

Versions successfully published, by artifact format (decision 21).

## `downloads_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Archive downloads folded into the durable counters by the rollup job.

## `search_reindex_documents_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Search documents written by the reindex job.

## `search_reindex_removed_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Search documents removed by the reindex job.

## `quarantine_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Upstream archives quarantined because their bytes did not hash to the digest the upstream advertised. Any non-zero value is worth a look: it is either a broken mirror or an attempted substitution.

## `upstream_drift_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Upstream versions whose bytes changed after we had cached them. The cached copy is kept and the alarm is raised; a published version's bytes are immutable, so drift is always a fact about the upstream, never about us.

## `shadowing_alarms_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Local package names that also exist upstream. Not an error — an operator decision about dependency confusion, which is why it is a signal and not a refusal.

## `upstream_versions_rejected_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Upstream version entries dropped during ingest as unusable or malformed.

## `upstream_fetch_total`

*counter*

Labels: `kind`, `outcome`

Upstream fetches by what was fetched and how it ended.

## `upstream_failure_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Upstream requests that failed, feeding the circuit breaker.

## `upstream_circuit_opened_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Times the upstream circuit breaker opened, stopping further fetches.

## `upstream_stale_served_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Responses served from an expired upstream cache entry because the upstream could not be reached — the graceful-degradation path, not an error.

## `cache_hit_ratio`

*gauge*

No labels.

Upstream cache hit ratio since start, 0..1.

## `upstream_sync_lag_seconds`

*gauge*

No labels.

Age of the last completed mirror sweep, in seconds. The number to alert on for a mirror-mode deployment: it grows without bound when the sweep stops.

## `blob_gc_scanned_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Blob keys examined by the garbage collector.

## `blob_gc_deleted_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Blobs deleted by the garbage collector.

## `blob_gc_bytes_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Bytes reclaimed by the garbage collector.

## `blob_gc_shards_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Archive shards swept to the end. A sweep walks the key space one shard at a time from a durable cursor, so this is the rate at which coverage rotates.

## `blob_gc_sweep_converged`

*gauge*

No labels.

1 when the last collector pass reached the end of the key space, 0 when it spent its budget first. Sustained 0 means passes never finish: raise `jobs.blob_gc.budget_secs` or lower the interval.

## `staging_sweep_scanned_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Staged-upload keys examined by the abandoned-upload sweep.

## `staging_sweep_deleted_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Abandoned staged uploads deleted. Steady state is roughly the rate of publishes that are started and never finished.

## `staging_sweep_bytes_total`

*counter*

No labels.

Bytes reclaimed from abandoned staged uploads.

## `queue_jobs_total`

*counter*

Labels: `kind`, `outcome`

Queue items that reached a terminal state, by job kind and outcome. `outcome="dead"` is work that will never be retried again.

## `queue_retention_deleted_total`

*counter*

Labels: `state`

Queue rows deleted by retention, by the terminal state they were in.

## `retention_deleted_total`

*counter*

Labels: `table`

Rows deleted by the S-23 retention pass, by table. `table="job_queue"` overlaps `queue_retention_deleted_total`, which breaks the same rows down by terminal state instead.

## `retention_refused_tables`

*gauge*

No labels.

Tables the database refused to let the retention pass delete from, as of the last pass. Non-zero means a table is growing without a bound and nothing else will say so: the expected cause is a Postgres provisioned per the hardened S-22 template without `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pub_audit_prune(TIMESTAMPTZ, INT)`. Alert on this — the pass keeps sweeping every other table, so no other signal changes.

## `retention_backlog_tables`

*gauge*

No labels.

Tables whose backlog outlived the last pass's wall-clock budget. Transient after a window is lowered or a backup is restored — the next pass continues. Persistently non-zero means `jobs.lifecycle` cannot keep up with the row rate.

## `retention_skipped_tables`

*gauge*

No labels.

Tables the last retention pass never reached, because its wall-clock budget was already spent by the tables ahead of them. Distinct from `retention_backlog_tables`: a table counted here is getting no retention at all rather than draining slowly. Persistently non-zero means `jobs.lifecycle.budget_secs` is too small for the instance's row rate.

## `queue_depth`

*gauge*

Labels: `kind`, `state`

Queue rows per kind and state, sampled each drain tick. A growing `pending` depth means the drain is slower than the enqueue rate.

## `mail_transport_unusable`

*gauge*

No labels.

1 when outbound mail cannot be delivered — the SMTP section will not build, or a send failed and none has succeeded since. Alert on this rather than on dead letters: with the shipped retry ladder a message needs ~21 minutes to die, and an OTP code expires in 10 (decision 29). Zero when no SMTP is configured at all, because delivering nothing to the in-memory sink is a success, not an outage.

## `notification_enqueue_failed_total`

*counter*

Labels: `event`

Domain events whose fan-out job could not be enqueued. Every one is a set of notifications nobody will ever receive.

## `notification_mail_enqueue_failed_total`

*counter*

Labels: `event`

Notification emails that could not be filed on the queue during fan-out.
